Definition: The number and activity level of technology hubs, incubators, accelerators, and co-working spaces focused on technology and innovation. These provide physical infrastructure and support for tech entrepreneurship and skills development.
Comments: None listed in AfriLabs/Briter Bridges 643 hubs report
revision_notes: Original score (1, None identified) cited only the 2019 AfriLabs/Briter Bridges 'A Hundred Hubs' report (mislabelled in the original Comments as a '643 hubs' report), which indeed does not list Eritrea. A fresh search found two identifiable operating entities not captured in continental trackers: the government/NUEYS-run Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Hub in Asmara (established 2023, delivering structured technical training and hosting national science and innovation fairs in 2024 and 2025, confirmed via the Eritrea Ministry of Information's shabait.com) and EriMT, a private co-working/business incubation space in Asmara that self-describes as Eritrea's first innovation hub and tech incubator (erimt.com; current operating status not independently reconfirmed beyond 2019). This meets the '1-2 hubs with limited activity' threshold, so the score is raised to 2. This is not a top-of-scale promotion (scale max is 5), so no escalation is required.
revised_comments: Eritrea's technology and innovation ecosystem remains at an early stage, with one to two identifiable hubs. The government-run Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Hub, established in 2023 under the National Union of Eritrean Youth and Students, delivers structured technical training (programming, robotics, electronics) to secondary-school students across all six regions and hosts an annual National Science and Innovation Fair. A private co-working and business incubation space, EriMT, also operates in Asmara, offering serviced offices and incubation support for entrepreneurs. Neither hub features in continental trackers such as AfriLabs or Briter Bridges, reflecting limited international visibility and modest scale of activity.

Definition: The country's e-government development level based on the UN E-Government Development Index (EGDI). This composite index measures online service delivery, telecommunications infrastructure, and human capital. Indicates the government's capacity to deliver digital public services.
revision_notes: Source cited (archive.assenna.com) is a 2017 news article restating the 2016 EGDI ranking (190/193, EGDI <0.25); this was accurate for its stated year. Checked the current UN EGDI dataset from the 2024 E-Government Survey (publicadministration.un.org/egovkb): Eritrea remains ranked 190th of 193 countries with an EGDI of 0.1576, still within the Low group (<0.25), alongside South Sudan and Somalia as the world's lowest performers. Score of 1 confirmed and updated to reflect the latest (2024) data; no change to the Value Code.
revised_comments: Eritrea ranks 190th of 193 countries on the UN E-Government Development Index (EGDI) in the 2024 UN E-Government Survey, with a score of 0.1576, placing it in the Low EGDI group (below 0.25) alongside South Sudan and Somalia among the world's lowest performers. The score reflects very limited online service provision, weak telecommunications infrastructure, and constrained human capital indicators.

Definition: The scale and quality of tertiary-level ICT and STEM education programmes available in the country, based on the number and quality of institutions offering ICT degrees, computer science programmes, and engineering courses relative to the population.
Value Name: Very limited (<2 institutions with ICT programmes)
Comments: Very limited, Eritrea Institute of Technology only [uniRank](https://www.unirank.org/er/uni/eritrea-institute-of-technology/)
revision_notes: Source cited (unirank.org) confirms Eritrea Institute of Technology (established 2003, Mai Nefhi) as the sole dedicated ICT/STEM tertiary institution. Cross-checked against a 2025 government report (shabait.com, Eritrea Ministry of Information) on the same institution, also known as Mai-Nefhi College of Engineering and Technology, confirming it remains active and is still the only institution offering ICT/STEM degree and diploma programmes in the country; no second qualifying institution was identified (other Eritrean tertiary colleges cover health sciences, business, agriculture and marine science, not ICT/STEM). Score of 1 confirmed and updated to reflect current (2025) evidence.
revised_comments: Tertiary ICT and STEM education in Eritrea is provided almost exclusively by the Eritrea Institute of Technology, also known as Mai-Nefhi College of Engineering and Technology, established in 2003 near Asmara. It is the country's only higher education institution offering computer science and related engineering degree and diploma programmes, spanning colleges of Science, Engineering and Technology, and Education. In its 2025 commencement it graduated 383 students, including 39 in Computer Science and Technology and 28 in Computer Application diploma studies. No other tertiary institution in Eritrea offers a comparable ICT or STEM programme.
